record.paper_title: Revisiting the foundations of the quantum theory of atoms in molecules: Some open problems
record.original_question: Can QTAIM be reformulated as a practical boundary-only theory in which calculations use only the two-dimensional interatomic surfaces and still yield the properties of the three-dimensional topological atoms, and what analytical differential geometry of interatomic surfaces is needed to make such a holographic formulation work?

evidence.quote: The next step will be to answer the question whether such holographic property may be used practically namely, one may derive a theory that only works with the inter-atomic surface, i.e. boundaries/2D surfaces, and yield the properties of the topological atoms without any need to refer to 3D space; this directs us toward the more general idea of duality [100-103].

Accordingly, the analytical differential geometry of the inter-atomic surfaces must be also considered more thoroughly [104-108], seeking for general traits of these surfaces that may help to apply the idea of the holography in practice.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\rho:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be a smooth scalar field (the electron density of a molecule), and let $\nabla\rho$ denote its gradient field. A point $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$ is called a critical point of $\rho$ if $\nabla\rho(x)=0$. A bond critical point is a critical point at which the Hessian of $\rho$ has signature $(-,-,+)$. The two eigenvectors of the Hessian with negative eigenvalues at a bond critical point span a two-dimensional unstable manifold of the gradient flow $\dot{x}=-\nabla\rho(x)$; the closure of this manifold is called an interatomic surface (IAS) $S$. The set of IASs partitions $\mathbb{R}^3$ into open regions $\{\Omega_A\}$ called topological atoms. Each $\Omega_A$ is a basin of attraction of a nuclear maximum of $\rho$ under the gradient flow, and its boundary $\partial\Omega_A$ is a union of IASs. By construction, every IAS satisfies the local zero-flux condition
$$\nabla\rho(x)\cdot n(x)=0\quad\text{for all }x\in S,$$
where $n(x)$ is the unit normal to $S$ at $x$.

For an observable represented by a real-valued density $f_A:\Omega_A\to\mathbb{R}$, define the atomic property
$$F(\Omega_A)=\int_{\Omega_A}f_A(x)\,dx.$$

Question. Provide an exact reformulation of the theory just described in which every atomic property $F(\Omega_A)$ is computed solely from data intrinsic to the two-dimensional boundary $\partial\Omega_A$ (its embedding, induced metric, second fundamental form, and the restriction of $\rho$ and its derivatives to $\partial\Omega_A$), without requiring any volume integral over $\Omega_A$ or any reference to the three-dimensional interior. Equivalently, exhibit, for a sufficiently large class of admissible densities $f_A$, a surface density $\sigma_A$ on $\partial\Omega_A$ such that
$$\int_{\Omega_A}f_A(x)\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega_A}\sigma_A\,dS,$$
where $\sigma_A$ is determined locally from the differential-geometric data of the IAS. In addition, develop the analytical differential geometry of IASs (regularity, principal curvatures, behavior near bond, ring, and cage critical points, global topological invariants, and the constraints imposed on these by the zero-flux condition) sufficient to make such a boundary-only ("holographic") formulation effective in practice.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns a conjectural holographic/boundary-only reformulation of the quantum theory of atoms in molecules and the development of the differential geometry of interatomic surfaces. No published general reformulation of QTAIM as a fully boundary-only theory, nor a comprehensive analytic differential-geometric theory of interatomic surfaces, appears to be established; the problem remains open as posed.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting the foundations of the quantum theory of atoms in molecules: Some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including whether QTAIM can be recast as a boundary-only (holographic) theory using only interatomic surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: The boundary-only reformulation of QTAIM is identified as an open problem requiring further differential-geometric analysis of interatomic surfaces.
